questions.question: What is a healthy Git workflow for a team?
questions.title: A Healthy Git Workflow
questions.direct_answer: A team workflow: 1) main is always deployable; 2) create a feature branch per task (git switch -c add-login); 3) make small, focused commits with clear messages (git commit -m 'add login form'); 4) push the branch (git push -u origin add-login); 5) open a pull request for review; 6) address review comments; 7) merge to main (or squash) after approval; 8) pull main regularly (git pull) to stay current. The rules: never commit directly to main, write messages in the imperative ('add' not 'added'), keep branches short-lived, and rebase or merge to incorporate main's changes. Small, reviewable PRs beat huge ones.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you describe branch-per-feature, small commits, PR review, and 'main is always deployable', and know the commands.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Committing straight to main, or huge long-lived branches that become hard to merge.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Branch per feature, small focused commits, PR for review, merge to main after approval. main is always deployable; never commit straight to main.
